previous_statement: Proposition 1.7 (Hayashi high probability): Given n copies of |psi> in C^d, Hayashi's algorithm outputs |v> with |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1-epsilon with probability >= 1-delta when n = O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon). Proof: The overlap |<v|psi>|^2 follows the Beta(1, d-1) distribution rescaled by (n+d)/(n+1) [ZS00]. By Skorski's Bernstein-type concentration bound for the Beta distribution [Sko23], Pr[|<v|psi>|^2 < 1-epsilon] <= exp(-n*epsilon/(2(d-1))) for epsilon < (d-1)/(n+d). Setting n = C*(d + log(1/delta))/epsilon for suitable constant C gives the result.
new_statement: Proposition 1.7 (Hayashi high probability): Given n copies of |psi> in C^d, Hayashi's algorithm outputs |v> with |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1-epsilon with probability >= 1-delta when n = O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon). Proof: The overlap |<v|psi>|^2 follows the Beta(n+1, d-1) distribution (not Beta(1,d-1), which describes a single Haar-random overlap). This follows because the Hayashi POVM element for outcome v has probability proportional to |<v|psi>|^{2(n+1)} times the Haar measure [ZS00]. The expected overlap is E[|<v|psi>|^2] = (n+1)/(n+d). For the concentration: Skorski's Bernstein-type bound for the Beta distribution [Sko23] (corrected for a sign error in the published lower-tail bound, as noted in the paper's lines 1512-1522) gives Pr[|<v|psi>|^2 < 1-epsilon] <= exp(-epsilon*n/2) for epsilon in (0, (d-1)/(n+d)). Setting n = C*(d + log(1/delta))/epsilon for a suitable constant C gives the failure probability <= delta.
